findings:
All eleven findings from the second review are now resolved, checked against the code. One new problem blocks approval. The critical ram starts by swinging the ship's nose onto the player, but the ship turns so slowly that the swing takes 4 to 12 seconds while the plan allows 3. The plan also doesn't say whether the ship then charges crooked or gives up, and one ram test can't pass as written. I would let the ram turn at the faster manoeuvring-jet rate, set its time limit from the config, and have it give up and retry when it still isn't aimed. The other seven findings are small corrections that one short edit can cover. Your last change request had no text, and the plan took it to mean "fix the second review's points". If you meant something else, please say so, because nothing else has been addressed.

| # | Severity | Problem | Fix | Tasks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | blocking | The ram's 3 s aiming step is shorter than the 4–12 s the hull needs to turn 90° onto a player beside it, what happens when time runs out is undefined, and ram row 5 can't pass. | Turn at the jets rate during line-up, size the cap from the config, return to hunting and retry if the nose is still off the aim at the cap, face the charge direction, and compare turn rates over the first 1 s. | t10 |
| P2 | minor | The torpedo's approach firing window is worked out from the hull centre, but the turret's arc test uses the tube, 196 px ahead, so the real window is about 1 s. | Correct the prose and the enemy doc to the tube's pivot, and optionally widen the tube's arc to about 100–110°. | t8, t12 |

### P1 — the ram can't finish aiming
`ram_line_up_cap` is 3.0 s and the line-up turns "at the current turn rates". In the Open Space orbit the player is abeam, so a ram starts about 90° off the nose. At 0.35 rad/s with both engines that is 4.5 s; listing toward the dead side (0.40) 3.9 s; toward the live side (0.125) 12.6 s; Assault listing on the live side 3.9 s. Only two Assault cases fit. The Ram Corvette's rule that "the charge follows the aim, not the nose" (its cap is 0.5 s on a nimble ship), copied here, would send a 448 px hull about 30° sideways off its own lane. That contradicts the lane drawn from the bow and the edge-limit corners oriented on the charge direction. Row 5 times two 90° turns, three of four over the cap. Rows 1–2 would still pass with a crooked charge, so the gate wouldn't catch it.

### P2 — torpedo window
From the tube's pivot, a player at hull distance 1100 on the tangent approach is about 47° off the nose, outside ±45°. The arc holds only between about 1257 and 1137 px of hull distance. No row asserts this, so nothing fails, but the documentation would be wrong.

### P3 — Assault upper leg off-screen
`ArenaCamera` (dead zone ±30, pan up to 380): with the player at y 650 the view top is y 260, while the upper leg's hull centre is at y 160. The fortress shares this.

### P4, P5 — missing plan sections
Section 2.4 only says to add the torpedo tube to the head list. The head's wiring and silhouette rules are in 2.3. The `kill_part()`, `ladder()` and `opts.ram` helpers are in 2.6.1. They are used by weapons rows 1, 5, 6 and 11, ram rows 1 and 4, and the interceptor task's weapon kills.

### P6 — hub lever
At 4800 px and 145°, the Heavy Gunship anchor is about 2331 px away. At 125°, the Laser Tender anchor is the same. Both are inside the 2500 px reach.

### P7 — gate-time margin
Phase 11's five fortress mounts added about 0.75 s to the fortress test file alone, and that task overran its allotment (1.8 s against 1.5 s). The Dreadnought builds eight mounts and about 80 rounds per spawn, in every earlier Dreadnought file and in both harnesses.

### P8 — charge length
`ram_speed × ram_max_time` = 1120 px. The orbit band is 700 ± 150, so at 850 px the charge ends before it gets 250 px past the player.
